cohort: 736 term neonates aged 3 to 12 days old with a weight > 2.5 kg and a gestational age > 37 weeks, referred to a neonatal clinic.
finding: Neonates born by normal vaginal deliveries showed more favorable outcomes regarding breastfeeding frequency, urination frequency, and first postpartum defecation time, while neonates born by caesarean sections had higher daily weight loss.
mod_finding: Neonates born by normal vaginal deliveries had more favorable breastfeeding, urination, and defecation patterns, and less daily weight loss compared to those born by caesarean sections.
cross-section timing: When neonates were 3 to 12 days old
